summary: Sunday's test-suite audit found that the nominal auto-merge gate can report success when the full unit suite fails, because its unittest process is piped through tail without pipefail. The audit also found two explainer depiction and sandbox guardrail modules that no runner actually collects, and a visual expression suite that is not a pre-merge requirement for every production-renderer change it is meant to protect. Both critical runtime alarms are already owned: explainer's zero-post outage remains under the active delivery-restoration strategy, and the August 22 trending repair failure predates the now-merged exchange-order fix. The broader test topology needs an explicit ownership inventory so adding a test file cannot silently create another decorative suite. Editorially, current trending evidence remains too stale and its reliability work too active for a new mix call, but Third now has a repeatable creator-level signal: three mature Plaqueboymax clips all cleared the doctrine floor and materially beat the channel median, supporting a bounded second-slot experiment without weakening any selection gate.

alarm_ack.no_posts_explainer: Already covered by open backlog aaeb12de3ebd, Restore explainer delivery before interpreting its topic test, ruled doing at critical severity.
alarm_ack.production_repair_trending: Already covered by open backlog e524811347c4, Auto-merge renders before the exchange handoff, which was in progress when the August 22 failure occurred; commit e9a8284 removed the premature direct Daily dispatch after that production date.

findings.title: The full unit gate discards unittest failures
findings.observation: The auto-merge job runs the full tests/ suite as `python -m unittest ... 2>&1 | tail -40` without enabling pipefail or checking PIPESTATUS. Bash therefore returns tail's zero status when unittest fails, the following steps continue, and the automerge job may squash-merge a branch whose unit suite is red. Replacing unittest with a process that exits 7 reproduces a pipeline status of zero under the same command shape.
findings.proposal: Enable pipefail for the step or capture the unittest output and explicitly propagate the test process status before printing its tail. Add a workflow-contract test that executes a deliberately failing producer through the exact reporting wrapper and requires the wrapper to return nonzero, so future log-format changes cannot reopen the bypass.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml lines 123-124 define the required Full unit suite step as `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2>&1 | tail -40` with no `set -o pipefail`; the job's scripts-suite step at lines 135-152 demonstrates the correct pattern by capturing each subprocess and explicitly setting `fail=1`. Running `bash -c 'python -c "raise SystemExit(7)" 2>&1 | tail -40'` on main returns status 0.

findings.title: Two explainer guardrail modules execute zero tests
findings.observation: The viz-director and viz-scene files contain free-function tests for no-bare-number selection, depiction fallbacks, unsafe mechanic rejection, and real frame rendering, but neither has unittest classes nor a script main. The repository's required suite discovers only tests/, while preview_explainer.yml invokes three other data_learning test files by name. Consequently unittest discovery under data_learning/tests collects zero tests from these modules, and `python -m` imports each module and exits successfully without executing a single assertion.
findings.proposal: Convert both modules to unittest-compatible cases or give them an explicit runner, then invoke them from the required explainer preflight. Add a collection-count assertion for the data_learning suite so a zero-test success is itself a failure.
findings.evidence: data_learning/tests/test_viz_director.py and data_learning/tests/test_viz_scene.py define only `test_*` functions and have no `if __name__ == '__main__'` runner; .github/workflows/preview_explainer.yml lines 53-60 runs showrunner scoring, repair loop, and mascot primitives but not either viz module. On current main, `python -m unittest discover -s data_learning/tests -p 'test_viz*.py' -v` reports `Ran 0 tests`, while both `PYTHONPATH=. python -m data_learning.tests.test_viz_director` and the equivalent viz_scene command exit 0 with no output.

findings.title: Expression visual proof is not a pre-merge renderer gate
findings.observation: The heavy expression tests are deliberately excluded from the auto-merge scripts suite and delegated to Expression Tests, but that separate workflow is not an upstream dependency of the squash merge. Its pull_request paths also omit data_learning/pro_render.py and scripts/test_expressions_render.py even though the push paths and comments identify the production renderer and render tests as part of this contract. A PR changing pro_render can therefore merge before any measured expression render runs; the visual proof starts only after the change has reached main.
findings.proposal: Make the expression suite a reusable required workflow called by the merge gate, or add a required pre-merge job that the automerge job explicitly needs. Align pull-request paths with the full push path set, including pro_render.py and test_expressions_render.py, and retain artifact upload for diagnosis after the status has been made merge-blocking.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/expression-tests.yml lines 20-35 include data_learning/pro_render.py in push paths but omit it from pull_request paths, and likewise omit scripts/test_expressions_render.py from both PR coverage and the declared commands. Lines 53-66 contain the actual render and measured-pixel proof. scripts/test_expressions.py and scripts/test_expressions_render.py are explicitly skipped by the main scripts-suite loop documented in .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml lines 130-142, leaving the separate workflow as their only intended gate.

findings.title: Govern every test file with an executable owner
findings.observation: The repository now has four incompatible test topologies: 63 unittest files under tests/, 41 standalone scripts/test_*.py programs, five data_learning test modules with mixed custom-main and pytest-style conventions, and eleven curiosity-nextgen modules discovered only by a channel-specific workflow. There is no repository-level assertion that every test-shaped file belongs to a runner or that its runner collected at least one test. The two currently orphaned viz modules are the concrete consequence: they look like tests in review but buy no protection.
findings.proposal: Define a declarative test-suite inventory that maps every test directory or file to its runner, dependency class, and required workflow. Extend the repository-layout gate to fail on an unowned test file, and make every runner emit and validate a nonzero collection count. Migrate incrementally toward one invocation convention while keeping expensive render suites as named shards rather than silently skipping them.
findings.evidence: tests/test_repo_layout.py checks Python placement and imports but has no test-owner inventory; data_learning/tests/test_pipeline.py implements its own `_main` collector, scripts/test_pipeline_health.py is a directly executed standalone test program, and experiments/curiosity_nextgen/tests/test_autonomous_core.py relies on a separate unittest-discovery command in curiosity-ci.yml. A filesystem count on current main finds 63 tests/test_*.py files, 41 scripts/test_*.py files, five data_learning/tests/test_*.py files, and eleven experiments/curiosity_nextgen/tests/test_*.py files, while no file records ownership across those runners.

findings.title: Give Plaqueboymax a bounded second-slot test
findings.observation: Third's August 23 analytics contain one creator with a repeated signal that clears the playbook's learning floor: three Plaqueboymax clips are each older than 24 hours, have 99-208 views and 51-116 engaged views, and retain 90.1%-93.7% on average. Their median velocity is 0.35 views per hour versus the channel's 0.04 all-video median. Other current top creators have only one clip each that meets all three maturity thresholds, so they are promising examples but not yet repeat evidence.
findings.proposal: For a bounded next-sample experiment, allow a second Plaqueboymax post on days with two genuinely separate events while preserving the existing six-slot target, one-creator default, novelty checks, and every quality gate. Tag the allocation decision, stop after five additional mature qualifying clips, and compare creator-level median velocity and retention before making any permanent source-priority change.
findings.evidence: state/analytics_third/latest.json was fetched at 2026-08-23T12:18:57Z and records the three qualifying Plaqueboymax videos: `No Budget` at 117 views/53 engaged/90.1% retention/0.46 VPH, `Five Gifted` at 208/116/93.7%/0.35, and `Get Feisty` at 99/51/93.6%/0.35; the same snapshot reports a channel median of 0.04 VPH. docs/THIRD_INTERNET_PLAYBOOK.md lines 230-238 permit a second same-streamer post for a separate major event, and lines 265-274 require at least 24 hours, 50 views, and 25 engaged views before learning from a video.
